I use iPhone Mirroring every day to quickly access my iPhone directly from my Mac, and this year's feature is about to get even better. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate have launched this month, bringing three important updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything that's new.

macOS 27: What's new in iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window for any iOS 27-compatible app. For now, this only applies to Apple's native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, support for window resizing will quickly expand.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: smaller, actual size, and larger. Changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

There are also several other updates to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Control Center access
  • DRM video support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring had no access to Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can use the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or access it through the "View" menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch copyright-protected videos through iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, when iPhone Mirroring was enabled, all DRM-protected videos would only display a black screen.

macOS 27 also provides a new app icon for iPhone Mirroring, just like many other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried them in the public beta? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
